title: Single Stock Lending UK
h1: Single Stock Lending UK (search-result title as shown in [a] and [b]; may be the <title> rather than the on-page H1 - not independently confirmed)
summary: Silver Oak Capital's single stock lending advisory page describes a loan secured against one specific equity holding (rather than a diversified portfolio) that lets the borrower raise money against a concentrated shareholding without selling the shares and while keeping ownership. Typical clients named are family offices, founders and majority shareholders who want to keep control of their stake. Structurally, shares are pledged to a third-party trustee; the borrower generally keeps voting rights (and upside) if covenants are met; loan-to-value ratios are lower and margin requirements stricter than for portfolio (Lombard) lending because of concentration risk. The page's FAQ states founders/insiders can use the product subject to insider-trading rules, pre-clearance requirements and contractual covenants, and lists risks: extra collateral may be required, shares may have to be partly sold to repay, and borrowing costs may be higher. The firm positions its network of specialist lenders as what gives clients access to this financing. No LTV percentage, rate, fee, loan size, duration or timescale was revealed for this page; no raw snippet text surfaced - all content arrived as the search tool's paraphrase.
